name: REMem

paper.title: REMem: Reasoning with Episodic Memory in Language Agent

construction.unit: gist (one time-stamped event sentence) + fact (triple with time qualifiers)
construction.kept_as: LLM-restated event sentences with resolved dates + extracted triples; raw messages kept as nodes
construction.processing: per session (LoCoMo) one LLM call writes gists, a second writes time-qualified triples from the text and the gists

organization.structure: hybrid graph: gist nodes, phrase nodes (fact subjects/objects), relation, context and gist synonymy edges
organization.stores: one graph with embedding stores for messages, gists, facts and phrases
organization.index: NV-Embed-v2 dense over gists and facts + BM25

management.operations: append only; synonymy edges between gists with similarity >= 0.8
management.conflicts: contradictory gists and facts are all kept as a history

retrieval.query: question on the first step; afterwards sub-queries and tool arguments written by the agent
retrieval.candidates: agent calls semantic (dense) or lexical (BM25) search, gist-context and entity-context graph tools with time filters
retrieval.selection: each call returns top-10 gists + top-10 facts; the agent decides when to stop
retrieval.budget: 3 steps (LoCoMo, REALTALK), 5 steps (Complex-TR, Test of Time); ~9k input tokens per LoCoMo query

use.context: question + whole agent history (thoughts, tool calls, retrieved gists and facts, draft answer)
use.reasoning: ReAct loop of tool calls, then one answer call

classify.note: REMem-S (single step) is a plain top-10 dense read; the headline REMem-I lets the agent choose tools and when to stop.

stages.ingestion: Conversations are fed one session at a time (LoCoMo, REALTALK) or one passage per event statement; each message is also stored as its own node.
stages.construction: An LLM restates each session as a list of single-event gists prefixed with the session timestamp and with relative dates resolved; a second call extracts (subject, predicate, object) facts with point-in-time or start/end qualifiers.
stages.organization: Gists and phrase nodes (fact subjects and objects) form one graph: facts link subject to object, each gist links to the phrases and facts from the same chunk, and gists with embedding similarity >= 0.8 get synonymy edges.
stages.update: Nothing is overwritten: new and contradictory items are added alongside old ones.
stages.retrieval: A ReAct agent (GPT-4.1-mini) calls semantic_retrieve, lexical_retrieve, find_gist_contexts or find_entity_contexts, each returning up to 10 gists and 10 facts, optionally filtered by time; at most 3 steps on conversation sets and 5 on reasoning sets.
stages.answer: When the agent calls output_answer, an answer LLM reads the question, the agent's draft answer and the full step history with every retrieved gist and fact.

summary: Episodic memory as a graph of time-stamped event gists and time-qualified triples, read by a tool-using agent that can filter by dates and walk the graph.
notes: Venue: ICLR 2026 poster (OpenReview forum fugnQxbvMm; PDF header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'). Code checked at commit d87840be (2026-02-27, the head of the repo); files stored with Git LFS (outputs, datasets) were not needed. Judge model is not named in the paper; the LoCoMo script uses the run's LLM (GPT-4.1-mini) with Mem0's judge prompt. The paper's LoCoMo category names differ from the Mem0 convention (see results notes).

sources.code_note: Commit d87840be (2026-02-27) is the current head and comes two days before paper v3; the repo was released with the paper, so it is taken as the evaluation code. Run outputs are not in the repo, so numbers could not be re-derived.

abstract.text: REMem targets episodic memory for language agents: recalling what happened when, and reasoning across several events on a timeline. It indexes experiences into a graph that mixes short time-stamped event gists with subject-predicate-object facts carrying time qualifiers. A ReAct-style agent then answers questions by calling retrieval and graph-exploration tools that can filter by time, over several steps. On LoCoMo, REALTALK, Complex-TR and Test of Time the authors report gains over Mem0, Graphiti and HippoRAG 2, largest on the reasoning sets, and better refusal on unanswerable questions.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

headline: The answer model reads LLM-written gists and triples plus the agent's own step history and draft answer; raw messages are stored but not shown.
REMem-S (one dense search, 10 gists + 10 facts) is best on LoCoMo LLM-J (77.5 vs 76.2); the multi-step agent wins on the reasoning sets (Test of Time EM 93.1 vs 72.5).
Gists are longer than the dialogue they come from: 21.7k gist tokens vs 16.0k input tokens per LoCoMo conversation (Table 22).

units.name: Gist node
units.role: one event from a session, as a standalone sentence
units.made_by: LLM gist prompt, one call per session

fields.name: gist text
fields.what: '[date, time] who did what …' with relative dates followed by the absolute date in parentheses

fields.name: gist embedding
fields.what: NV-Embed-v2 vector of the gist text

units.name: Fact
units.role: time-scoped triple; its subject and object become phrase nodes
units.made_by: LLM fact prompt, reads the session and its gists

fields.name: subject, predicate, object
fields.what: schemaless short phrases, e.g. (Alice, purchased, 3 cows)

fields.name: qualifiers
fields.what: record_time plus point_in_time or start_time / end_time

units.name: Message node
units.role: one original message of the session

fields.name: verbatim message
fields.what: the raw turn with speaker and date
fields.src: code episodic_gist_strategy.py L94-L114; answer_generator.py L182, L280-L309 (verbatim context off by default)

write.how: one chunk per session with its date on top; messages also split into separate nodes
LLM restates every fact or event as one sentence prefixed with the session timestamp and resolves relative dates
LLM extracts triples with time qualifiers from the session text and its gists
subject → object edge per fact; each gist → the phrases and facts of its chunk; each message → its gists and phrases
gist-to-gist edges when embedding similarity ≥ 0.8 (at most ~100 per gist)

read.input: the full question (the tool's query argument is overridden)
read.scores: gist text and fact text + qualifiers
read.how: agent must start with semantic or lexical retrieve
ReAct: the agent picks one of five tools per step from the question and the history so far
start/end time with lt/le/ge/gt/eq filters facts by their qualifiers; gists are not filtered
a separate answer call over the step history

answer_context.sees: question, the agent's draft answer, and every step's thought, tool call, observation and up to 10 gists and 10 facts (each cut at 1,500 characters)
answer_context.format: 'Question: …' + 'Preliminary Answer (for reference)' + 'Agent Interaction History: Step n: {reasoning, function, parameters} - Truncated top gists / facts'

compression.what: per-query input tokens, REMem-I vs full context on LoCoMo
compression.basis: §5.1: Full-Context uses 26k input tokens per LoCoMo query, REMem-I 9k and REMem-S 0.9k at inference

compression.what: gist text vs source text, one LoCoMo conversation
compression.basis: Not a reduction: Table 22 reports 21,743.8 gist-node tokens vs 15,965.8 input tokens per graph, so gists are about 1.36x longer than the input

paper_vs_code.paper: two node types: gists and phrases (App. B)
paper_vs_code.code: also message (verbatim) nodes and fact nodes linked to gists

paper_vs_code.paper: the tool explores gists linked by synonymy edges
paper_vs_code.code: graph edges are added with only a weight attribute, while the tool keeps neighbours whose edge predicate contains 'synonym'; as released it seems to return linked facts but no synonym gists (not run by us)

paper_vs_code.paper: retrieval tools filter memory by temporal conditions
paper_vs_code.code: semantic and lexical retrieve filter only facts; gists are ranked without the filter

open_questions: REMem-S beats REMem-I on LoCoMo LLM-J, so on conversational recollection the gain over baselines comes from the gist index rather than from agentic retrieval.
Baselines retrieve 10 raw messages; REMem sees 10 gists + 10 facts per step for up to 3-5 steps, so context size is not matched.

discussion.takeaway: Storing conversations as time-stamped event gists plus time-scoped triples, and letting an agent query them with date filters, helps most when questions need reasoning across several events on a timeline.

claims.claim: REMem beats state-of-the-art memory systems on episodic recollection.
claims.evidence: LoCoMo LLM-J 77.5 (REMem-S) / 76.2 (REMem-I) vs 74.0 HippoRAG 2 and 73.0 NV-Embed-v2; REALTALK 65.3 vs 59.5. Table 3

claims.claim: The gain is larger on episodic reasoning.
claims.evidence: Complex-TR LLM-J 89.6 vs 81.5 (HippoRAG 2); Test of Time EM 93.1, the only method above 90. Table 4, Table 13

claims.claim: Multi-step tool use matters for reasoning.
claims.evidence: REMem-I over REMem-S: LLM-J +7.0 on Complex-TR, EM +20.6 on Test of Time. §5.2

claims.claim: Gists carry most of the signal; facts help multi-hop.
claims.evidence: without gists LoCoMo LLM-J 76.2 → 48.9; without facts Complex-TR 89.6 → 87.2 and LoCoMo multi-hop −7.1. Table 5, App. C.6

claims.claim: REMem refuses unanswerable questions more reliably.
claims.evidence: refusal F1 64.0 vs 53.1 Graphiti and 13.5 Mem0 on 446 LoCoMo adversarial questions. Table 6

limits: Tested on conversation and temporal reading benchmarks, not on agents acting in complex environments.
Memory is built by offline batch indexing; building it as a stream is left open.
Error analysis: wrong value on the right slot (46%), temporal or numeric slips (19%) and abstaining despite retrieved evidence (18%) on LoCoMo.
reading: On LoCoMo the single-step REMem-S has the higher LLM-J (77.5 vs 76.2), and the paper notes most questions need one session; the agent pays 10x the inference tokens (18.1M vs 1.83M input) for no gain there.
Baselines retrieve 10 raw messages (HippoRAG 2: 3 sessions), while REMem reads 10 gists + 10 facts per step for up to 3-5 steps, so context sizes differ.

The paper's LoCoMo category names follow a different id mapping from Mem0's: its 'Single-Hop' (321) and 'Temporal' (96) are ids 2 and 3, which Mem0-style papers call temporal and open-domain. Per-category numbers cannot be compared across papers by name.
LoCoMo scores include the 446 adversarial questions in the average (1,986 questions), unlike papers that report 1,540.
The judge is the run's own LLM (GPT-4.1-mini in the code) with Mem0's prompt; the paper does not name the judge model.
Gist text per conversation (21.7k tokens) exceeds the source (16.0k), so this is re-expression, not compression.

At the released commit, find_gist_contexts looks for edges labelled 'synonym' but synonymy edges carry no label, so the tool may never return similar gists; yet removing synonymy edges changes scores (Table 5), which suggests the paper's runs used different code or the edges act elsewhere.
